name: PA-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+11 partisan lean
Kelly's huge financial advantage ($1.3M cash vs $38K)
No polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: Kelly combines a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge, while markets give Wagner about a 5% chance. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Kelly or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Pennsylvania's 16th District leans strongly Republican, and six-term incumbent Mike Kelly is seeking another term with the full weight of that advantage behind him. Kelly has raised nearly $1.2 million and holds about $1.3 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Justin Wagner has raised under $70,000 with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets give Kelly roughly a 94% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's R+11 lean, Kelly's incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. Wagner would need an extraordinary shift in the political environment to threaten the seat, and nothing in the available evidence points to one.
